Energy transition

Load Shedding

The coal fleet keeps breaking down. Diesel can cover some of the gap, but it cannot make the problem cheap to ignore.

Play Load Shedding↗ See what’s at stake ↓

Free to play in your browser. Choose your difficulty in the game.

Location
Johannesburg, South Africa
Starts in
2016
Your term
7 years

The situation

Your starting point

You start in 2016 with a scaled South African fleet dominated by coal, alongside a little nuclear, diesel, wind and solar power. Much of the coal equipment is already decades old.

Over the scenario, coal availability falls as breakdowns outpace repairs. Waiting leaves you with less usable power and a growing need for expensive emergency fuel. Replacement plants take time to finish.

The choices

What will you do?

  1. 01

    Build against declining output

    Plan around the coal fleet's available power, not its nameplate capacity. Each drop in output leaves more work for the rest of your system.

  2. 02

    Use diesel deliberately

    Emergency generation can keep customers supplied, but fuel purchases quickly consume cash. Decide what it should bridge and when that bridge should end.

  3. 03

    Make the replacement last

    Choose a mix that covers demand throughout the day and stays affordable to operate. Avoid replacing one concentrated vulnerability with another.

Put your plan to the test

Can your new capacity arrive faster than the old fleet loses its ability to deliver?

Build, watch what happens, and try a different approach. The grid is yours to run.
